action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

# Agent Brain Benchmark Harness

> **Status: internal working records, not product claims.**
>
> This directory is the harness and its retained runs, kept so results stay
> auditable and reproducible. Much of what is retained here records what could
> *not* be substantiated: runs marked `no_release_claim`, comparisons rejected
> for confounds, and claims that were demoted after review.
>
> That is deliberate. Keeping a failed or withdrawn measurement is how the next
> person avoids repeating it. **None of it is a performance claim about Entire
> Brain**, and the product documentation deliberately makes no benchmark claims.
> `mise run release:matrix` prints which tracks are citable and which are not.

This directory contains a repeatable harness for comparing Codex and Claude Code
with and without Entire Brain.

For unpaid product-path latency and packet-size profiling without an agent or
model, use `profile_brief.py` with the 114-task checked-in development corpus.
See `BRIEF-PROFILE-BASELINE.md`. That profile is explicitly not confirmatory and
does not measure code quality.

For an unpaid, same-query comparison of the MCP `brain_brief` `legacy_json` and
opt-in `compact_v1` packet formats, use `packet_format_ab.py`. See
`PACKET-FORMAT-AB.md`. It checks parseability, compact-packet integrity,
independently projected semantic parity, exact bytes, and a frozen offline token
proxy. Report schema 2 also retains numeric-only, exact structural byte
attribution for future packet-format design. It does not call an agent/provider,
measure code quality, authorize a paid trial, or change either MCP or CLI
defaults.

For the independently parsed `compact_v2` design, use
`packet_format_v2_ab.py`; see `PACKET-FORMAT-V2-AB.md`. It additionally checks
the in-band `~`/`^` legend, exact keyed schemas and types, same-opcode reference
scope, and the deterministic strictly-shorter per-family wire-form choice.
Its fixed 114-task byte/token-proxy gates and privacy/authorization limits are
the same as the v1 comparison. Report schema 2 also binds the exact runner,
corpus verifier, product contract, golden, schema/allowlist, legend, and gates
through a path-free hash-only runner identity.

For the smaller opt-in `compact_v3` product serializer and its scoped
public/synthetic fixture evidence, see
[`PACKET-FORMAT-V3-LOCAL-MEASUREMENT.md`](PACKET-FORMAT-V3-LOCAL-MEASUREMENT.md).
That local measurement covers exact packet bytes and `o200k_base` tokens only;
it is not a run over the private 114-task corpus and makes no quality claim.

Checked-in historical evidence is a publication-safe derivative rather than a
byte-identical copy of private producer artifacts. See
[`PUBLICATION-SANITIZATION.md`](PUBLICATION-SANITIZATION.md) for the exact scope,
integrity treatment, and retained synthetic credential fixture.

## Treatment-isolated tasks

Confirmatory tasks use `user_query`, an explicit `retrieval_query_source` (`user_query` or
`oracle_queries`), and a `treatments` object keyed by condition. Treatment arms are `no_memory`,
`placebo_packet`, `retrieved_memory`, and the upper-bound-only `oracle_retrieval`. Comparable arms
must use the WIP harness-owned `frozen_brief` delivery; their agent-visible instruction is identical and differs only inside the
`<frozen-memory-packet>` payload. Oracle queries are harness-owned and never written to `prompt.txt`.

Legacy `prompt` and `brain_queries` tasks remain runnable for reproducing exploratory suites, but
legacy `frozen_brief` delivery may still consume `brain_queries` harness-side. Those queries are not
agent-visible, and legacy tasks fail confirmatory panel preflight. A confirmatory panel must set
`"confirmatory": true`; every included task also needs
an `approved_symptom_only` entry in `task-review-ledger.json`. Automated task-validity lint is triage,
not human approval. The historical 8828752a7 and 4dd458656 prompts are retained under
`fixtures/task-validity/` and explicitly excluded as oracle-assisted.

Run deterministic triage and validate the review ledger without an agent/model call:

```sh
python3 run.py lint-tasks --tasks fixtures/task-validity/oracle-assisted-regressions.json
```

## Stable panel (`panel`) + the stability gate

"Is benchmarking stable?" is answered with a **committed panel manifest** plus a **printed
per-task verdict**, not ad-hoc flags:

```sh
python3 run.py panel full          # runs panels/full.json, prints a stability verdict per task/condition

grade.py
guides
parse.py
questions
run-all.sh
run.sh
runs
setup-guides.sh

test_git_shim.py
test_parse.py
# Memory ladder

A small, reproducible comparison of what a coding agent can answer about a
repository's past as you add memory surfaces one step at a time:

| Cond | Agent has | Guide the agent receives |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | source tree and git history | plain note; no Entire tooling |
| 2 | + hosted session history (`entire search`, `entire checkpoint explain --full`) | plain note + session section |
| 3 | + Graph (`entire graph query`, `neighbors`, `impact`) | `entire graph agent-guide` rendered outside a repository (standalone Graph) + session section |
| 4 | + Brain, normal guidance | Brain's `agent-guide --normal` rendered inside this repository (combined Graph and Brain) + session section |
| 5 | + Brain, strict guidance | this repository's committed `.entire/agent-guide.md` + session section |

Every condition runs the same prompt against a fresh clone with the same
read-only tool allowlist. The harness directory itself (prompt, rubric, this
README) is removed from the clone's worktree and HEAD tree before the agent
starts, so it cannot read its own answer key. Once the harness has merged it still
exists in history, so the agent's `git` is also a shim (`bin/git`): read
subcommands only, any argument naming the directory refused, and a pathspec
exclusion appended to history and content readers so `git show <sha>` and
`git log -p` cannot print its diff even for the commits that added it. Mixed
commits can still expose harness details in their messages. `parse.py` records
any probe for the directory and marks a run contaminated if a tool result
carries harness identifiers (including commit metadata), rubric or README
content; `grade.py` excludes those. The clone's
HEAD is one commit past the indexed commit, and Brain's freshness label moves from
"degraded" to "unsafe"; its facts and history sections are unchanged by that
(checked: 3 facts and 3 history matches before and after). A shim first on `PATH` decides which `entire`
subcommands exist, so an agent cannot reach a surface its condition excludes,
and lifecycle hooks are swallowed so nested runs never capture checkpoints. The
guides are generated from the product at run time, not checked in.

The question is the kind a product manager asks, not an engineer: "should we
auto-activate Brain on global install, and was this decided before?" Its
recorded answer exists only in agent session history and as a Brain
closed-negative fact, not in code, docs or commit messages.

## Run it

Requirements: `claude` (Claude Code CLI), `entire` logged in (hosted search needs

content.content:
Eval runs a held-out task set through a selected retriever and reports, per task and
	in aggregate: retrieved items, estimated tokens, precision, recall when labels
	exist for that retriever, and useful-items-per-1k-tokens (the headline agent
	metric).

The tasks file is a JSON array:
  [{"id":"t1","task":"how does X work","branch":"main","k":10,
    "relevant":["fact:abc","fact:def"],"label_source":"human"}]
			With retriever-specific "relevant" ids, metrics are deterministic. Generated
			source-session labels give source-match credit for history/preprocessed-session
			arms but do not define recall. Without labels, pass --judge to have the agent
			decide relevance per surfaced item. With source-session tasks, pass
			--judge --judge-source-matches to replace source-overlap proxy credit with
			judge-labeled relevance for history/preprocessed-session arms.

Usage:
  entire-brain memories eval --tasks <file> [flags]

Flags:
      --agent string                Judge/expand agent: auto, codex, claude-code, ollama, or command (default "auto")
      --agent-command stringArray   Agent command argv for --agent command
      --arm string                  Fact retrieval arm: flat, scoped, scoped-floor, or outline (default "flat")
      --branch string               Default branch for tasks that omit one (default: current branch)
      --expand                      Expand each task query with agent-generated retrieval terms before retrieval
      --expand-cache string         Persist/reuse query expansions at this path
  -h, --help                        help for eval
      --json                        Emit the summary as JSON
      --judge                       Use the agent to judge relevance when a task has no labels
      --judge-cache string          Persist/reuse judge verdicts at this path so re-runs are deterministic and cheap
      --judge-source-matches        With --judge, judge source-match proxy rows instead of counting transcript/session overlap as relevance
      --k int                       Facts to retrieve per task (default 10)
      --model string                Model for codex/claude-code/ollama judge and expand calls
      --retriever string            Retrieval arm: facts, history, query, or raw-sessions (default "facts")
      --semantic                    Rerank with the local embedding backend (RRF fusion of lexical + semantic)
      --tasks string                Path to the held-out task set (JSON array)
---GEN
eval-gen turns the brain into a self-labeled benchmark: each captured session
	becomes a task (its opening user request), and the facts whose provenance points

- Store paths and skill writes: `internal/cli/env.go`, `path.go`, `safe_read.go`, `skill_form.go`, `memory_state_io*.go`.
- Subprocesses and unattended work: `internal/cli/runner.go`, `distill_cmd.go`, `watch.go`, `hook_cmd.go`, `internal/entityindex/graphdiff.go`.
- MCP scope and bounds: `internal/cli/mcp.go`, `retrieval_transport.go`, `semantic_stream.go`.
- Checkpoint export and source privacy: `internal/cli/export.go`, semantic ignore filtering, transcript handling.
- Shared identities and transport: `factmerge/`, `internal/factsync/`, `internal/hostedbrain/`, `internal/brainwire/`, `internal/factgitmeta/`.
- Benchmark isolation and provenance: `benchmarks/agent-brain/`.

1. Code execution from untrusted repository/config/transcript/provider content. Trace git external diff, textconv, filters, fsmonitor, subprocess argv/env, and agent/provider selection. Honor explicit user-configured command execution without extending it to untrusted inputs.

Eval runs a held-out task set through a selected retriever and reports, per task and
	in aggregate: retrieved items, estimated tokens, precision, recall when labels
	exist for that retriever, and useful-items-per-1k-tokens (the headline agent
	metric).

The tasks file is a JSON array:
  [{"id":"t1","task":"how does X work","branch":"main","k":10,
    "relevant":["fact:abc","fact:def"],"label_source":"human"}]
			With retriever-specific "relevant" ids, metrics are deterministic. Generated
			source-session labels give source-match credit for history/preprocessed-session
			arms but do not define recall. Without labels, pass --judge to have the agent
			decide relevance per surfaced item. With source-session tasks, pass
			--judge --judge-source-matches to replace source-overlap proxy credit with
			judge-labeled relevance for history/preprocessed-session arms.

Usage:
  entire-brain memories eval --tasks <file> [flags]

Flags:
      --agent string                Judge/expand agent: auto, codex, claude-code, ollama, or command (default "auto")
      --agent-command stringArray   Agent command argv for --agent command
      --arm string                  Fact retrieval arm: flat, scoped, scoped-floor, or outline (default "flat")
      --branch string               Default branch for tasks that omit one (default: current branch)
      --expand                      Expand each task query with agent-generated retrieval terms before retrieval
      --expand-cache string         Persist/reuse query expansions at this path
  -h, --help                        help for eval
      --json                        Emit the summary as JSON
      --judge                       Use the agent to judge relevance when a task has no labels
      --judge-cache string          Persist/reuse judge verdicts at this path so re-runs are deterministic and cheap
      --judge-source-matches        With --judge, judge source-match proxy rows instead of counting transcript/session overlap as relevance
      --k int                       Facts to retrieve per task (default 10)
      --model string                Model for codex/claude-code/ollama judge and expand calls
      --retriever string            Retrieval arm: facts, history, query, or raw-sessions (default "facts")
      --semantic                    Rerank with the local embedding backend (RRF fusion of lexical + semantic)
      --tasks string                Path to the held-out task set (JSON array)

content.content:
# Durable Facts Plan

This plan describes how Entire Brain can grow from a read-only derivation layer
over captured sessions into a curated, branch-aware, blameable **durable fact
memory** — without abandoning the property that makes Entire's data trustworthy:
source-backed facts are views over retained session/checkpoint source, not
standalone artifacts you have to trust. Authored facts are explicit user
assertions and must be reported as such when no retained source is attached.

Entire already captures more raw context than most agent-memory systems: full
session transcripts, checkpoints tied to commits, multiple agents, rewind and
resume. Entire Brain already *derives* read-only history records and decisions
from that corpus. What is missing is a distilled, deduplicated, agent-writable
fact layer that survives across sessions, is scoped to a branch, and can be
traced back to retained anchors today. Full cryptographic turn-level proof still
depends on future Entire CLI turn signing.

## Core Principle: Derive And Cite, Never Extract And Discard

Other agent-memory systems extract a fact with an LLM and keep only the
extracted text. The source turn is gone, so the fact cannot be re-derived,
audited, or verified — it must simply be trusted.

Entire retains checkpointed ground-truth sessions. Therefore source-backed
durable facts in this design are **views over retained source**:

- **Re-derivable** — a source-backed fact can be regenerated from its cited
  session/checkpoint/transcript source.
- **Blameable** — a fact points to the retained anchors it has today: session,
  checkpoint, transcript path/line, commit where available, and turn id where
  captured.
- **Verifiable** — current verification checks local checkpoint/export/session
  consistency at the granularity available today. Full cryptographic turn-level
  verification still depends on future CLI-side turn signing.

This gives the value of curated, versioned, branch-aware memory *plus*
local auditability that extract-and-discard systems structurally cannot offer.
Entire Brain does not need its own Merkle/cryptographic store for this layer:
checkpoint/export anchors can be checked locally now, and future turn signing
can tighten the verification boundary without changing fact storage.

## Goals

- Add an agent-writable, curated fact store (`remember` / `recall`) layered on
  the existing brain, with the same on-disk inspectability as other brain
  sources.
- Add a batch `distill` pass that turns captured Entire sessions into durable
  facts under a strict quality gate, instead of relying on per-turn capture.
- Classify facts into a stable, shallow taxonomy so `brief`, `recall`, and
  unified `search` / `query` results stay precise as the corpus grows.
- Scope facts to a branch and promote/merge them when the code branch merges.
- Give every fact provenance: blame to retained session/checkpoint anchors, with
  local verification now and cryptographic turn verification after CLI-side turn
  signing lands.
- Add embedding-based recall over the fact layer only (a small, high-value
  corpus), keeping the brain's "not a code vector DB" stance intact.

## Non-Goals

- Do not introduce a separate cryptographic versioned store. Provenance reuses

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * *" # 06:00 UTC daily, matching entire-graph
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

  group: nightly
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # Only cut a nightly when main actually moved. A dated prerelease per day that
  # nothing changed is noise, and it makes "which nightly has the fix" harder to
  # answer, not easier.
  changed:
    name: has main moved
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4
    outputs:
      should_release: ${{ steps.check.outputs.should_release }}
      version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sha="$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
          base="$(grep -oE '^## +\[?v?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' CHANGELOG.md 2>/dev/null \
                    | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' || true)"
          [[ "$base" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]] || base="0.1.0"
          version="v${base}-nightly.$(date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M).${sha}"

          # Skip when the newest prerelease already points at this commit.
          latest="$(gh release list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --limit 1 \
                     --json tagName --jq '.[0].tagName // ""' 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if [[ "$latest" == *".${sha}" ]]; then
            echo "main has not moved since $latest — skipping"
            echo "should_release=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "should_release=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          echo "version=${version}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  build:
    name: nightly build
    needs: changed
    if: needs.changed.outputs.should_release == 'true'
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

# Agent Brain Benchmark Harness

> **Status: internal working records, not product claims.**
>
> This directory is the harness and its retained runs, kept so results stay
> auditable and reproducible. Much of what is retained here records what could
> *not* be substantiated: runs marked `no_release_claim`, comparisons rejected
> for confounds, and claims that were demoted after review.
>
> That is deliberate. Keeping a failed or withdrawn measurement is how the next
> person avoids repeating it. **None of it is a performance claim about Entire
> Brain**, and the product documentation deliberately makes no benchmark claims.
> `mise run release:matrix` prints which tracks are citable and which are not.

This directory contains a repeatable harness for comparing Codex and Claude Code
with and without Entire Brain.

For unpaid product-path latency and packet-size profiling without an agent or
model, use `profile_brief.py` with the 114-task checked-in development corpus.
See `BRIEF-PROFILE-BASELINE.md`. That profile is explicitly not confirmatory and
does not measure code quality.

For an unpaid, same-query comparison of the MCP `brain_brief` `legacy_json` and
opt-in `compact_v1` packet formats, use `packet_format_ab.py`. See
`PACKET-FORMAT-AB.md`. It checks parseability, compact-packet integrity,
independently projected semantic parity, exact bytes, and a frozen offline token
proxy. Report schema 2 also retains numeric-only, exact structural byte
attribution for future packet-format design. It does not call an agent/provider,
measure code quality, authorize a paid trial, or change either MCP or CLI
defaults.

For the independently parsed `compact_v2` design, use
`packet_format_v2_ab.py`; see `PACKET-FORMAT-V2-AB.md`. It additionally checks
the in-band `~`/`^` legend, exact keyed schemas and types, same-opcode reference
scope, and the deterministic strictly-shorter per-family wire-form choice.
Its fixed 114-task byte/token-proxy gates and privacy/authorization limits are
the same as the v1 comparison. Report schema 2 also binds the exact runner,
corpus verifier, product contract, golden, schema/allowlist, legend, and gates
through a path-free hash-only runner identity.

For the smaller opt-in `compact_v3` product serializer and its scoped
public/synthetic fixture evidence, see
[`PACKET-FORMAT-V3-LOCAL-MEASUREMENT.md`](PACKET-FORMAT-V3-LOCAL-MEASUREMENT.md).
That local measurement covers exact packet bytes and `o200k_base` tokens only;
it is not a run over the private 114-task corpus and makes no quality claim.

Checked-in historical evidence is a publication-safe derivative rather than a
byte-identical copy of private producer artifacts. See
[`PUBLICATION-SANITIZATION.md`](PUBLICATION-SANITIZATION.md) for the exact scope,
integrity treatment, and retained synthetic credential fixture.

## Treatment-isolated tasks

Confirmatory tasks use `user_query`, an explicit `retrieval_query_source` (`user_query` or
`oracle_queries`), and a `treatments` object keyed by condition. Treatment arms are `no_memory`,
`placebo_packet`, `retrieved_memory`, and the upper-bound-only `oracle_retrieval`. Comparable arms
must use the WIP harness-owned `frozen_brief` delivery; their agent-visible instruction is identical and differs only inside the
`<frozen-memory-packet>` payload. Oracle queries are harness-owned and never written to `prompt.txt`.

Legacy `prompt` and `brain_queries` tasks remain runnable for reproducing exploratory suites, but
legacy `frozen_brief` delivery may still consume `brain_queries` harness-side. Those queries are not
agent-visible, and legacy tasks fail confirmatory panel preflight. A confirmatory panel must set
`"confirmatory": true`; every included task also needs
an `approved_symptom_only` entry in `task-review-ledger.json`. Automated task-validity lint is triage,
not human approval. The historical 8828752a7 and 4dd458656 prompts are retained under
`fixtures/task-validity/` and explicitly excluded as oracle-assisted.

Run deterministic triage and validate the review ledger without an agent/model call:

```sh
python3 run.py lint-tasks --tasks fixtures/task-validity/oracle-assisted-regressions.json
```

## Stable panel (`panel`) + the stability gate

"Is benchmarking stable?" is answered with a **committed panel manifest** plus a **printed
per-task verdict**, not ad-hoc flags:

```sh
python3 run.py panel full          # runs panels/full.json, prints a stability verdict per task/condition

# Memory ladder

A small, reproducible comparison of what a coding agent can answer about a
repository's past as you add memory surfaces one step at a time:

| Cond | Agent has | Guide the agent receives |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | source tree and git history | plain note; no Entire tooling |
| 2 | + hosted session history (`entire search`, `entire checkpoint explain --full`) | plain note + session section |
| 3 | + Graph (`entire graph query`, `neighbors`, `impact`) | `entire graph agent-guide` rendered outside a repository (standalone Graph) + session section |
| 4 | + Brain, normal guidance | Brain's `agent-guide --normal` rendered inside this repository (combined Graph and Brain) + session section |
| 5 | + Brain, strict guidance | this repository's committed `.entire/agent-guide.md` + session section |

Every condition runs the same prompt against a fresh clone with the same
read-only tool allowlist. The harness directory itself (prompt, rubric, this
README) is removed from the clone's worktree and HEAD tree before the agent
starts, so it cannot read its own answer key. Once the harness has merged it still
exists in history, so the agent's `git` is also a shim (`bin/git`): read
subcommands only, any argument naming the directory refused, and a pathspec
exclusion appended to history and content readers so `git show <sha>` and
`git log -p` cannot print its diff even for the commits that added it. Mixed
commits can still expose harness details in their messages. `parse.py` records
any probe for the directory and marks a run contaminated if a tool result
carries harness identifiers (including commit metadata), rubric or README
content; `grade.py` excludes those. The clone's
HEAD is one commit past the indexed commit, and Brain's freshness label moves from
"degraded" to "unsafe"; its facts and history sections are unchanged by that
(checked: 3 facts and 3 history matches before and after). A shim first on `PATH` decides which `entire`
subcommands exist, so an agent cannot reach a surface its condition excludes,
and lifecycle hooks are swallowed so nested runs never capture checkpoints. The
guides are generated from the product at run time, not checked in.

The question is the kind a product manager asks, not an engineer: "should we
auto-activate Brain on global install, and was this decided before?" Its
recorded answer exists only in agent session history and as a Brain
closed-negative fact, not in code, docs or commit messages.

## Run it

Requirements: `claude` (Claude Code CLI), `entire` logged in (hosted search needs

Eval runs a held-out task set through a selected retriever and reports, per task and
	in aggregate: retrieved items, estimated tokens, precision, recall when labels
	exist for that retriever, and useful-items-per-1k-tokens (the headline agent
	metric).

The tasks file is a JSON array:
  [{"id":"t1","task":"how does X work","branch":"main","k":10,
    "relevant":["fact:abc","fact:def"],"label_source":"human"}]
			With retriever-specific "relevant" ids, metrics are deterministic. Generated
			source-session labels give source-match credit for history/preprocessed-session
			arms but do not define recall. Without labels, pass --judge to have the agent
			decide relevance per surfaced item. With source-session tasks, pass
			--judge --judge-source-matches to replace source-overlap proxy credit with
			judge-labeled relevance for history/preprocessed-session arms.

Usage:
  entire-brain memories eval --tasks <file> [flags]

Flags:
      --agent string                Judge/expand agent: auto, codex, claude-code, ollama, or command (default "auto")
      --agent-command stringArray   Agent command argv for --agent command
      --arm string                  Fact retrieval arm: flat, scoped, scoped-floor, or outline (default "flat")
      --branch string               Default branch for tasks that omit one (default: current branch)
      --expand                      Expand each task query with agent-generated retrieval terms before retrieval
      --expand-cache string         Persist/reuse query expansions at this path
  -h, --help                        help for eval
      --json                        Emit the summary as JSON
      --judge                       Use the agent to judge relevance when a task has no labels
      --judge-cache string          Persist/reuse judge verdicts at this path so re-runs are deterministic and cheap
      --judge-source-matches        With --judge, judge source-match proxy rows instead of counting transcript/session overlap as relevance
      --k int                       Facts to retrieve per task (default 10)
      --model string                Model for codex/claude-code/ollama judge and expand calls
      --retriever string            Retrieval arm: facts, history, query, or raw-sessions (default "facts")
      --semantic                    Rerank with the local embedding backend (RRF fusion of lexical + semantic)
      --tasks string                Path to the held-out task set (JSON array)
---GEN
eval-gen turns the brain into a self-labeled benchmark: each captured session
	becomes a task (its opening user request), and the facts whose provenance points
	back to that session are provenance/silver labels. These labels are useful for
	recall-oriented measurement, but hand labels or --refine are still required
	before precision/recall release claims. Each task is tagged with a query-type
	stratum (code/convention/howto/concept). Emits a tasks.json consumable by
	'facts eval --tasks'.

	--source sessions emits tasks directly from exported sessions, including sessions
	with zero distilled facts. Those tasks have source anchors but no relevance labels,
	so use --judge or human labels before making relevance claims.

	--refine judge-filters each task's provenance label set with the agent, keeping
only facts genuinely relevant to the request — trading the recall-oriented "every
session fact" labels for precision-clean ones (verdicts cached for reuse).

Usage:
  entire-brain memories eval-gen [flags]

Flags:
      --agent string                Agent for --refine: auto, codex, claude-code, ollama, or command (default "auto")
      --agent-command stringArray   Agent command argv for --agent command
      --branch string               Limit to one branch (default: all branches with facts)
  -h, --help                        help for eval-gen
      --judge-cache string          Persist/reuse --refine verdicts at this path
      --limit int                   Cap the number of tasks, sampled evenly across strata (0 = all)
      --max-facts int               Skip broad sessions with more relevant facts than this (diffuse targets); 0 = no cap (default 30)
      --min-facts int               Minimum relevant facts for a session to become a task (default 2)
      --model string                Model for codex/claude-code/ollama refine calls
      --out string                  Write tasks JSON to this file (default: stdout)
---RUNNERS

Review changes on branch "{{branch}}" vs "{{base_branch}}". Follow the actual data flow to distinguish exploitable defects from speculation.

# Threat model (read first)

Treat repository content/config, git attributes/config, branch and repo keys, checkpoint metadata/transcripts, provider snapshots, MCP arguments, synthesized skill names, and hosted responses/shared fact sets as untrusted input.

Central invariant: indexing, recalling, or synchronizing a hostile repository must not execute unintended code, escape the intended store or repository, disclose secrets, or let one member silently substitute another member's facts. Explicit user-configured agent/provider commands are intentional execution boundaries; distinguish those from commands derived from untrusted data.

Preserve the existing descend-only path and symlink guards, canonical-versus-derived storage boundary, brain write locks, atomic publication, identity validation, and repository scope. Check actual implementation rather than assuming an open hardening PR has already landed.

# What to run

1. `git diff <base-ref>...HEAD --stat`, then the full diff.
2. go.mod / go.sum for new or changed deps, `replace` directives, loosened pins, alternate proxies.
3. .github/workflows/ and mise.toml for changes that download or execute external code or expose secrets.
4. Grep the diff for the sink surfaces below and read the surrounding code.

# Sensitive surface (prioritize)

- Store paths and skill writes: `internal/cli/env.go`, `path.go`, `safe_read.go`, `skill_form.go`, `memory_state_io*.go`.
- Subprocesses and unattended work: `internal/cli/runner.go`, `distill_cmd.go`, `watch.go`, `hook_cmd.go`, `internal/entityindex/graphdiff.go`.
- MCP scope and bounds: `internal/cli/mcp.go`, `retrieval_transport.go`, `semantic_stream.go`.
- Checkpoint export and source privacy: `internal/cli/export.go`, semantic ignore filtering, transcript handling.
- Shared identities and transport: `factmerge/`, `internal/factsync/`, `internal/hostedbrain/`, `internal/brainwire/`, `internal/factgitmeta/`.
- Benchmark isolation and provenance: `benchmarks/agent-brain/`.

# Vulnerability classes (adversarial, in priority order)

1. Code execution from untrusted repository/config/transcript/provider content. Trace git external diff, textconv, filters, fsmonitor, subprocess argv/env, and agent/provider selection. Honor explicit user-configured command execution without extending it to untrusted inputs.
2. Path traversal or symlink/TOCTOU escapes in reads, writes, skill installation, or recursive deletion. Check bare `..`, absolute paths, Windows drives/UNC, symlinked roots, and every store-path construction site.
3. Credential or content disclosure through logs, errors, export, or hosted sync; ignored/private paths must stay excluded. Check destination selection and authentication scope.
4. MCP cross-repository access or deletion without explicit permission, HTTP request path injection, unsafe transport, SSRF, or weakened authorization.
5. Shared fact forgery or wire-contract ambiguity: content-derived IDs, proposal binding, canonicalization, and provenance must retain their actual guarantees.
6. Supply-chain and CI changes: untrusted dependencies/replacements, unpinned downloads/actions, widened credentials, or repository code executing with secrets.
7. Resource exhaustion: unbounded file/device reads, frames, decompression, allocations, provider calls, or cancellation that leaves a process or lock alive.
8. Benchmark isolation escapes, answer-key access, or untrusted packet content crossing prompt delimiters.

Weight findings by whether untrusted input actually reaches the sink: a boundary merely touched is Moderate; untrusted data reaching exec/path/egress without validation is High-to-Critical.

- 0-10 Clean: no security-relevant changes.
- 11-25 Low: minor changes near a boundary, no clear risk.
- 26-50 Moderate: security-relevant code touched (exec, path, MCP, sync, auth).
- 51-70 Elevated: suspicious patterns in exec, path, egress, or credential paths.
- 71-85 High: untrusted data reaching exec/path/egress without validation.
- 86-100 Critical: clear ACE/RCE, arbitrary file write via traversal, credential/data exfiltration, or cross-repository destruction.

This plan describes how Entire Brain can grow from a read-only derivation layer
over captured sessions into a curated, branch-aware, blameable **durable fact
memory** — without abandoning the property that makes Entire's data trustworthy:
source-backed facts are views over retained session/checkpoint source, not
standalone artifacts you have to trust. Authored facts are explicit user
assertions and must be reported as such when no retained source is attached.

Entire already captures more raw context than most agent-memory systems: full
session transcripts, checkpoints tied to commits, multiple agents, rewind and
resume. Entire Brain already *derives* read-only history records and decisions
from that corpus. What is missing is a distilled, deduplicated, agent-writable
fact layer that survives across sessions, is scoped to a branch, and can be
traced back to retained anchors today. Full cryptographic turn-level proof still
depends on future Entire CLI turn signing.

## Core Principle: Derive And Cite, Never Extract And Discard

Other agent-memory systems extract a fact with an LLM and keep only the
extracted text. The source turn is gone, so the fact cannot be re-derived,
audited, or verified — it must simply be trusted.

Entire retains checkpointed ground-truth sessions. Therefore source-backed
durable facts in this design are **views over retained source**:

- **Re-derivable** — a source-backed fact can be regenerated from its cited
  session/checkpoint/transcript source.
- **Blameable** — a fact points to the retained anchors it has today: session,
  checkpoint, transcript path/line, commit where available, and turn id where
  captured.
- **Verifiable** — current verification checks local checkpoint/export/session
  consistency at the granularity available today. Full cryptographic turn-level
  verification still depends on future CLI-side turn signing.

This gives the value of curated, versioned, branch-aware memory *plus*
local auditability that extract-and-discard systems structurally cannot offer.
Entire Brain does not need its own Merkle/cryptographic store for this layer:
checkpoint/export anchors can be checked locally now, and future turn signing
can tighten the verification boundary without changing fact storage.

## Goals

- Add an agent-writable, curated fact store (`remember` / `recall`) layered on
  the existing brain, with the same on-disk inspectability as other brain
  sources.
- Add a batch `distill` pass that turns captured Entire sessions into durable
  facts under a strict quality gate, instead of relying on per-turn capture.
- Classify facts into a stable, shallow taxonomy so `brief`, `recall`, and
  unified `search` / `query` results stay precise as the corpus grows.
- Scope facts to a branch and promote/merge them when the code branch merges.
- Give every fact provenance: blame to retained session/checkpoint anchors, with
  local verification now and cryptographic turn verification after CLI-side turn
  signing lands.
- Add embedding-based recall over the fact layer only (a small, high-value
  corpus), keeping the brain's "not a code vector DB" stance intact.

## Non-Goals

- Do not introduce a separate cryptographic versioned store. Provenance reuses

---NIGHTLY
name: nightly

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * *" # 06:00 UTC daily, matching entire-graph
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: nightly
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # Only cut a nightly when main actually moved. A dated prerelease per day that
  # nothing changed is noise, and it makes "which nightly has the fix" harder to
  # answer, not easier.
  changed:
    name: has main moved
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4
    outputs:
      should_release: ${{ steps.check.outputs.should_release }}
      version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sha="$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
          base="$(grep -oE '^## +\[?v?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' CHANGELOG.md 2>/dev/null \
                    | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' || true)"
          [[ "$base" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]] || base="0.1.0"
          version="v${base}-nightly.$(date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M).${sha}"

          # Skip when the newest prerelease already points at this commit.
          latest="$(gh release list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --limit 1 \
                     --json tagName --jq '.[0].tagName // ""' 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if [[ "$latest" == *".${sha}" ]]; then
            echo "main has not moved since $latest — skipping"
            echo "should_release=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "should_release=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          echo "version=${version}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  build:
    name: nightly build
    needs: changed
    if: needs.changed.outputs.should_release == 'true'
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

- Store paths and skill writes: `internal/cli/env.go`, `path.go`, `safe_read.go`, `skill_form.go`, `memory_state_io*.go`.

2. Path traversal or symlink/TOCTOU escapes in reads, writes, skill installation, or recursive deletion. Check bare `..`, absolute paths, Windows drives/UNC, symlinked roots, and every store-path construction site.

under this workload. Full method, variance and caveats are in [scale](scale.md).
Re-run the benchmark to evaluate your current build and corpus.

## Retrieval quality: what moved the numbers

> **Superseded 2026-10-12:** semantic retrieval was removed entirely. A
> 1,748-run live-agent eval across two repositories, three models, and corpus
> sizes up to 1,209 facts measured an in-process BM25 ranker with taxonomy
> filters matching or beating the full embedder stack on recall and precision
> while cutting agent tokens 18-28%, per-query memory 96% (316 MB -> 14 MB in
> the prototype measurement), and 31 MB off every binary. The rows below are
> retained as the historical record that gated earlier ship decisions; the
> superseding row and its caveats (a marginal haiku-class recall edge for the
> embedder, p=0.051) are in the [eval ledger](eval_ledger.md), and the
> implementation is tracked in trail #278. The doc source was measured only
> indirectly: its lexical-only ranking after the removal is an inference from
> the facts result, not a doc-side eval.


These are Brain measured against Brain — one retrieval arm against another on
the same corpus and task set. They are not comparisons with other products.

| Finding | Evidence | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BM25 over substring matching on history | 2.7x–5.1x useful/1k across strata on entire-cli; BM25 gains also observed on two other repositories | BM25 is the no-embedder default |
| EmbeddingGemma fusion over BM25 | +13% useful/1k (t=7.08) and precision +0.016 (t=7.68) at 418k records / 2,584 tasks; replicated at +12.5% (t=5.09) on a second repo | Fused history arm ships, gated on a configured Gemma-class embedder |
| Semantic fusion on facts | +0.459 useful/1k (p=0.005, Holm-significant), precision +0.025, no token cost, n=121 | Fusion default-on for `recall` and `brief` |
| Locus-scoped retrieval | +59% useful/1k (p=0.027 raw, marginal under Holm), −112 tokens (p<0.001), recall −0.029 | Scoped retrieval shipped; outline kept as a map, not a ranker |

Full rows, task sets and corpus identities are in the [eval ledger](eval_ledger.md).

## Agent outcome: one proof-ready result

Retrieval metrics measure retrieval. Whether a brain changes what an agent
*does* is a different question, and a much harder one to answer honestly.

**One measurement has passed our proof gate.** A correctness task whose decided
value exists only in retained history, run five times per side with
`claude:sonnet:high` in the retained August 2026 panel:

| Condition | Validation pass rate |
| --- | ---: |
| no brain | **0 / 5** |
| semantic_history_brain (history channel) | **5 / 5** |

`proof_ready=true` — the lift survives drop-one — with **0 hard integrity flags**
and 20/20 records provenance-backed across the two tasks in the panel. Without the brain the agent cannot recover
the exact decided value; with it, it reads it from history and restores it.

This flipped the history-channel correctness scope from no-claim to claimable.
It is one task on one repository with n=5 per side, scoped to this runner and
history channel. The other task saturated at 5/5 in both arms and is not proof
of lift. The [retained audit](../benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/replay-lab-clean/codex-audit-report.md)
and its manifest are checked by `mise run clean-proof:evidence`. This narrow
result does not establish MCP, Radar, codex-runner, or efficiency agent lift.

## What we deliberately do not claim

Brain's benchmark evidence runs under a **claim policy with an auditor that
refuses citations that have not earned them**. Most retained evidence sits in
`no_release_claim` mode on purpose:

```
claim_policy: no_release_claim
proof_ready_comparisons: 0
```

`mise run release:evidence` fails if a claim-bearing suite is not
provenance-complete, audit-clean, backed by a stable proof-ready comparison, and
run at least four times per side against the *current* task definitions.

So the MCP, Radar, codex-runner and efficiency scopes have numbers, and we do
not cite them. They have not passed the gate. The retained artifacts are kept
specifically so an auditor can see why they are not citable yet.

A clean no-claim audit validates the disclosure; it does not establish an
agent-quality improvement. The separate history-channel lane above has its own
proof-required gate.

## Closed negatives

Things we tried, measured, and dropped. A benchmark page with no losses on it
is a marketing page.

- **Query expansion.** An early d≈0.47 was an n≈8 artifact; at n=121 it
  collapsed to d=0.10, p=0.26. Stays opt-in.
- **Model2Vec fusion on history.** Significantly *worse* than BM25 on precision
  at production scale (t=−6.33 on 418k records, t=−2.84 on a second repo) with
  no useful/1k gain. A promising small-repo +31% was noise.
- **Conversation-exchange fusion.** Traded exact-match precision for one extra
  paraphrase hit. Ships dark behind a flag; `query` stays BM25-only.
- **RRF fusion-weight tuning.** Swept; every cell within noise. Equal weight,
  k0=60 stands.
- **Facts FTS5 BM25 as default.** Parity, not better (1.43 vs 1.50). Opt-in.
- **Scoped-floor via backfill facts.** Dead end.

## Head-to-head against other products

We have not run one.

A defensible head-to-head would need the same corpus, the same task set, the
same judge, and the same token accounting on both sides, with enough repetitions
to survive drop-one — the bar our own claim gate applies. Published numbers from
memory products are generally measured on their own corpora with their own
scorers, so quoting them side by side with ours would compare two different
experiments and call it a comparison.

What we can say from measurement rather than assertion:

- **Historical scale costs are substantial**, as [above](#scale-historical-measurements);
  a comparison against another implementation remains unmeasured.

---
name: brain-four-condition-demo-experiment
description: Memory-ladder experiment (benchmarks/memory-ladder, PR #336): 2026-10-06 sessions-only beat Brain because of brief --json layout; after the #337 fix (merged 2026-10-07) Brain recovered a fresh recorded decision 3/3 vs sessions 0/3, fastest and cheapest
metadata:
  type: project
---

Karthik asked for a reproducible ladder demo of Entire Brain: no Entire tooling / hosted sessions / + Graph / + Brain normal guide / + Brain strict guide, same question, fresh clones, Sonnet headless, 3 reps. Harness lives in benchmarks/memory-ladder (PR #336, trail 251). It supports LADDER_BRAIN_BIN to test a Brain build that is not the installed plugin (shim execs it for `entire brain`; reads the installed store).

Run 1 (2026-10-06, question: auto-activate Brain on global install): sessions 3/3, Brain 0/3. Cause: `brief --json` put a ~12.8 KB status block before facts/history and agents truncated; `query` returned only docs in hybrid mode (docs get two RRF lists, facts one). Issue #335; fix PR #337 (brief order + guides name `recall`) merged 2026-10-07.

Run 2 (2026-10-07, question: should the brief's action checklist put the exact failing test first; ground truth fact:0eb17dd880339fde70d888ca, source session 019f8699 line ~24053): code+git 0/3, sessions 0/3, +Graph 0/3, Brain normal 3/3 (mean 26 s, 160k input tokens, 6-8 tool calls, every run called recall first), Brain strict 3/3 (mean 115 s, 260k tokens). Sessions-only agents found the right session via hosted search but did not read the transcript.

**Why:** This is the measured answer to "does Brain add value over plain sessions"; the earlier proof-ready 0/5 vs 5/5 compares memory vs no memory, not Brain vs sessions.

**How to apply:** For demos, use the memory-ladder with a question whose rationale is session-only and not discussed in recent sessions (check with hosted `entire search` and repo grep first; Brain ingests live sessions so anything discussed today contaminates tomorrow). Facts are branch-scoped: recall/brief on a feature branch see no facts; use `--branch main` or clone main. `query` ranking is still open on #335.
---
Requirements: `claude` (Claude Code CLI), `entire` logged in (hosted search needs
it), `entire graph` and `entire brain` plugins installed, a clean checkout.

```sh
benchmarks/memory-ladder/run-all.sh            # 3 reps x 5 conditions, sequential, then grade
benchmarks/memory-ladder/run.sh 2 1            # one condition, one rep
python3 benchmarks/memory-ladder/grade.py      # table of runs and per-condition means
```

The clone is single-branch and non-local: the source repository carries Entire's
checkpoint refs, whose commits are session transcripts (including those of the
sessions that built this harness and quote its answer key), and a default clone
would expose them to every condition through `git log --all`. Only the branch
under test and tags are fetched, and the checkpoint objects are not transferred.

The agent is confined to its clone. Measured against this Claude Code build:
Bash file commands (`cat`, `find`, `ls`, `grep`) on a path outside the working
directory are blocked by the runtime; the Read tool is not, so it is granted only
as `Read(./**)`; the Grep and Glob tools are not path-scoped by permission rules,
so they are not granted and the agent uses `grep`, `rg`, `find` and `ls` through
the sandboxed shell; the Agent tool launches regardless of the allowlist and
cannot be scoped to one subagent type, so it is denied (subagents inherited the
parent's rules when measured, and no run so far launched one). Runs land in `$TMPDIR/memory-ladder-runs` by default and
`run.sh` refuses an output directory inside this repository, so the clone never
sits a relative path away from the un-stripped harness. `parse.py` records every
tool input that names a path outside the clone and marks a run contaminated if
one reaches the source repository.

Knobs: `LADDER_BRAIN_BIN` (an `entire-brain` binary to run instead of the
installed plugin for conditions 4 and 5, for example a build from `main`; it
reads the installed store and also renders condition 4's guide), `LADDER_MODEL`
(default `sonnet`), `LADDER_MAX_TURNS` (80), `LADDER_OUT`
(default `$TMPDIR/memory-ladder-runs`, must be outside this repository), `LADDER_ORIGIN` (clone origin URL; Brain and
Graph derive the repository key from it, so keep the GitHub URL), `LADDER_BRANCH`
(default `main`; Brain scopes facts to the checked-out branch, so a clone of a
feature branch sees no facts at all). Graph prewarm
for conditions 3 and above is excluded from timing and recorded in `prewarm.txt`.

Each run leaves `stream.jsonl` (the full agent transcript), `summary.json`
(metrics, completion state, every shell command, the final answer, the clone's
HEAD) and the clone it ran in. `grade.py` averages completed runs only and lists
failed or capped runs separately.
Add a question by dropping `questions/<name>.txt` and
`questions/<name>.rubric.json`; the rubric is named regexes over the final answer
and its `recovered` key is a first pass that should be hand-checked.

## Questions

- `global-activation`: should global plugin install auto-activate Brain in every
  repository, and was that decided before? Recorded answer: tried, called a
  regression, reversed; lives in one session and one closed-negative fact.
- `test-first-checklist`: should the brief's action checklist put the exact
  failing test first? Recorded answer: tried, rejected after it cost about 31%
  more tokens and 27% more time under semantic tolerance; lives in one session
  (deep in a 16k-line transcript) and one closed-negative fact. Chosen for the
  second run because the first question had been discussed in sessions by then.

## Run 2 (2026-10-07): after the #335 fix, question `test-first-checklist`

Brain built from `main` at the merge of #337 via `LADDER_BRAIN_BIN`; three
repetitions; Sonnet.

| Cond | Recovered | Mean duration | Mean input tokens | Mean tool calls |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 code + git | 0/3 | 24 s | 179k | 9 |
| 2 + sessions | 0/3 | 38 s | 213k | 8 |
| 3 + Graph | 0/3 | 52 s | 224k | 11 |
| 4 + Brain, normal | **3/3** | 26 s | 160k | 7 |
| 5 + Brain, strict | **3/3** | 115 s | 260k | 11 |

Every normal-guide Brain run called `recall` first and cited the fact with its
session, checkpoint and transcript line. Sessions-only runs found the right
session through hosted search and explained five other checkpoints from it, but
never the one carrying the measurement, and none read a transcript with
`--full`; two said so. Conditions 1 and 3 reported no evidence, correctly. The
strict guide reached the same answer at four times the wall clock, mostly
preflight and Graph impact calls.

## Run 1 (2026-10-06): before the fix, question `global-activation`

Three repetitions per condition, Sonnet, this repository at `main`. "Recovered"

agentName: Brain trail runners for effectiveness evaluation

content.text:
Yes. And the gap is sharper than "it would be nice": every piece of a Brain self-evaluation already exists in this repo, and none of them is wired to a trail.

**What exists today**

- Seven runners in `.entire/runners/`: review, drift, confidence, risk, security, summary, semantic-diff. Every one of them scores the diff. None asks "does recall or brief still give the right answer after this change?"
- An offline evaluator, `entire-brain memories eval --tasks`, that reports precision, recall and useful-items-per-1k-tokens. With labeled tasks it is deterministic and needs no model call.
- A self-labeling generator, `memories eval-gen`, that turns the brain's own sessions into tasks with provenance labels.
- The memory-ladder harness, which is a live-agent Brain-vs-sessions comparison and gave the 3/3 vs 0/3 result.
- The confirmatory harness with its claim gate, which is paid, slow, and by design refuses to emit claims casually.

**Why this matters, concretely**

Issue #335 is the proof. A brief layout change put a 12.8 KB status block ahead of facts, agents truncated, and Brain went from useful to 0/3 recovered. It merged, and a demo run found it a day later. A deterministic eval runner on that trail would have scored it before merge. Brain's own benchmark docs say retrieval regressions are the thing you should fear most, and then nothing guards them per trail.

**What I would build, in order**

1. **Retrieval regression runner** (push-triggered, unpaid). Build the branch binary, run `memories eval` over a frozen labeled task set against a checked-in fixture store, run the same against the base binary, emit the delta as a trail monitor. Polarity higher-is-better on useful/1k, plus a hard floor on recall. This is the #335 catcher.
2. **Packet usefulness runner** (observational, cheap model). Read the trail's own session transcripts, find the brief and recall calls, and judge whether the agent used or cited what came back versus ignored it. This is Brain evaluated from its own exhaust, and it generalises to customer repos, which makes it the product story: Trails, Runners and Brain in one loop.
3. **Memory-ladder smoke** (api-triggered only). One question, condition 4 vs condition 2, branch binary via `LADDER_BRAIN_BIN`. Needs hosted login and plugins in the sandbox, so keep it on demand.

**Two constraints to respect**

- These are regression signals, not evidence. The repo's claim policy requires n≥4 per side and drop-one survival before anything is citable. A runner score must never be read as "Brain is X% better".
- Facts are branch-scoped, so a runner on a feature branch sees no facts unless it passes `--branch main` or uses a fixture store. Semantic retrieval is gone since trail #278, so labels must be BM25-era.

**Assumption I have not verified:** that the prompt_runner sandbox can build Go and hold a brain store. If it cannot, runner 1 falls back to a packaged nightly binary and a synthetic fixture, which the publication-sanitization work already produces.

  files        Write durable memories out as plain Markdown files you can grep, read and diff

// evalTaskResult is the per-task measurement. The headline metric is
// UsefulPer1k — relevant items surfaced per 1,000 tokens spent — which captures
// the Appendix D agent constraint (value per token, not item count).
type evalTaskResult struct {
	ID                 string  `json:"id"`
	Task               string  `json:"task"`
	QueryType          string  `json:"query_type,omitempty"`
	Retriever          string  `json:"retriever,omitempty"`
	RelevanceSource    string  `json:"relevance_source,omitempty"`
	Surfaced           int     `json:"surfaced"`
	Tokens             int     `json:"tokens"`
	LatencyMS          int64   `json:"latency_ms"`
	ExpansionLatencyMS int64   `json:"expansion_latency_ms"`
	EndToEndLatencyMS  int64   `json:"end_to_end_latency_ms"`
	RelevantSurfaced   int     `json:"relevant_surfaced"`
	Precision          float64 `json:"precision"`
	Recall             float64 `json:"recall"`
	UsefulPer1k        float64 `json:"useful_per_1k"`
	Labeled            bool    `json:"labeled"`
	LabelSource        string  `json:"label_source,omitempty"`
}

// evalStratum aggregates metrics for one query-type stratum.
type evalStratum struct {
	Tasks           int     `json:"tasks"`
	MeanTokens      float64 `json:"mean_tokens"`
	MeanPrecision   float64 `json:"mean_precision"`
	MeanUsefulPer1k float64 `json:"mean_useful_per_1k"`
}

type evalSummary struct {
	Retriever              string                 `json:"retriever,omitempty"`
	Arm                    string                 `json:"arm,omitempty"`
	RunConfig              *evalRunConfig         `json:"run_config,omitempty"`
	Tasks                  int                    `json:"tasks"`
	MeanTokens             float64                `json:"mean_tokens"`
	MeanLatencyMS          float64                `json:"mean_latency_ms"`
	MeanExpansionLatencyMS float64                `json:"mean_expansion_latency_ms"`
	MeanEndToEndLatencyMS  float64                `json:"mean_end_to_end_latency_ms"`
	MeanPrecision          float64                `json:"mean_precision"`
	MeanUsefulPer1k        float64                `json:"mean_useful_per_1k"`
	ByStratum              map[string]evalStratum `json:"by_stratum,omitempty"`
	SurfacedByKind         map[string]int         `json:"surfaced_by_kind,omitempty"`
	Results                []evalTaskResult       `json:"results"`
}

type evalRunConfig struct {
	TasksPath             string `json:"tasks_path,omitempty"`
	TasksSHA256           string `json:"tasks_sha256,omitempty"`
	BrainManifestSHA256   string `json:"brain_manifest_sha256,omitempty"`
	Branch                string `json:"branch,omitempty"`

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Retrieval regression probe for Entire Brain.

Builds an isolated brain store from a committed fixture, runs the labeled
`memories eval` facts retriever and a `brief` packet probe against it, and
compares the branch binary with the base-branch binary. The result is a
0-100 trail monitor value plus a one-line rationale.

This is a regression signal, not evidence. See README.md for what it does
and does not claim.

Subcommands:
  freeze   seed the fixture with one binary and write fixture/tasks.json
  measure  seed + eval + brief probe for one binary, print the report
  compare  build HEAD and a base ref, measure both, print report and monitor
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
FIXTURE_DIR = HERE / "fixture"
FACTS_PATH = FIXTURE_DIR / "facts.json"
QUESTIONS_PATH = FIXTURE_DIR / "questions.json"
TASKS_PATH = FIXTURE_DIR / "tasks.json"

# A brief packet whose facts key sits past this fraction of the bytes is the
# #335 shape: a status block ahead of the evidence, which truncating agents
# never reach.
BRIEF_PREFIX_LIMIT = 0.5


class ProbeError(RuntimeError):
    """A step that makes the measurement meaningless (build, seed, contract)."""


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# helpers


def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
    return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def load_json(path: Path) -> Any:
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        return json.load(fh)


def run(argv: list[str], *, cwd: Path, env: dict[str, str], timeout: int = 300) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    return subprocess.run(
        argv,
        cwd=str(cwd),
        env=env,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=timeout,
        check=False,
    )


def git_env(base: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Git with no user or system config: no hooks, no entire checkpoints."""
    env = dict(base)
    env["GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL"] = os.devnull
    env["GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM"] = os.devnull
    env["GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT"] = "0"
    return env


def repo_root() -> Path:
    out = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
        cwd=str(HERE),
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    )
    return Path(out.stdout.strip())


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# isolated store


class FixtureStore:
    """A throwaway repository plus plugin dirs that one binary writes into."""

    def __init__(self, root: Path, origin: str, branch: str) -> None:
        self.root = root
        self.repo = root / "repo"
        self.xdg = root / "xdg"
        self.origin = origin
        self.branch = branch

    def create(self) -> None:
        self.repo.mkdir(parents=True)
        for name in ("config", "data", "state", "cache"):
            (self.xdg / name).mkdir(parents=True)
        env = git_env(os.environ.copy())
        steps = [
            ["git", "init", "-q", "-b", self.branch],
            ["git", "remote", "add", "origin", self.origin],
            [
                "git",
                "-c",
                "user.name=fixture",
                "-c",
                "user.email=fixture@example.invalid",
                "commit",
                "-q",
                "--allow-empty",
                "-m",
                "retrieval regression fixture",
            ],
        ]
        for argv in steps:
            proc = run(argv, cwd=self.repo, env=env)
            if proc.returncode != 0:
                raise ProbeError(f"fixture git step failed: {' '.join(argv)}: {proc.stderr.strip()}")

    def env(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        env = git_env(os.environ.copy())
        env["ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT"] = str(self.repo)
        env["ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CONFIG_DIR"] = str(self.xdg / "config")
        env["ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR"] = str(self.xdg / "data")
        env["ENTIRE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR"] = str(self.xdg / "state")
        env["ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR"] = str(self.xdg / "cache")
        env.pop("ENTIRE_BRAIN_SESSION_ID", None)
        return env

    def brain(self, binary: Path, *args: str, timeout: int = 120) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        return run([str(binary), *args], cwd=self.repo, env=self.env(), timeout=timeout)


def seed(store: FixtureStore, binary: Path, facts: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Record every fixture fact; return key -> fact id."""
    ids: dict[str, str] = {}
    for fact in facts["facts"]:
        proc = store.brain(
            binary,
            "remember",
            fact["text"],
            "--path",
            fact["path"],
            "--kind",
            fact["kind"],
            "--branch",
            store.branch,
            "--agent",
            "none",
            "--json",
        )
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise ProbeError(f"remember failed for {fact['key']}: {proc.stderr.strip()[:300]}")
        try:
            payload = json.loads(proc.stdout)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
            raise ProbeError(f"remember emitted no JSON for {fact['key']}: {exc}") from exc
        fact_id = str(payload.get("id") or "").strip()
        if not fact_id:
            raise ProbeError(f"remember returned no id for {fact['key']}")
        ids[fact["key"]] = fact_id
    return ids


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# measurement


def eval_facts(store: FixtureStore, binary: Path, tasks_path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    proc = store.brain(
        binary,
        "memories",
        "eval",
        "--tasks",
        str(tasks_path),
        "--retriever",
        "facts",
        "--branch",
        store.branch,
        "--agent",
        "none",
        "--json",
        timeout=300,
    )
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        raise ProbeError(f"memories eval failed: {proc.stderr.strip()[:300]}")
    try:
        return json.loads(proc.stdout)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
        raise ProbeError(f"memories eval emitted no JSON: {exc}") from exc


def brief_probe(store: FixtureStore, binary: Path, tasks: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Does the brief packet carry the labeled facts, and how far in do they sit?"""
    rows = []
    for task in tasks:
        proc = store.brain(binary, "brief", task["task"], "--branch", store.branch, "--json")
        raw = proc.stdout
        row: dict[str, Any] = {"id": task["id"], "ok": proc.returncode == 0, "bytes": len(raw.encode("utf-8"))}
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            row["error"] = proc.stderr.strip()[:200]
            row["hit"] = False
            row["prefix_fraction"] = 1.0
            rows.append(row)
            continue
        try:
            packet = json.loads(raw)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            row.update({"ok": False, "error": "brief emitted no JSON", "hit": False, "prefix_fraction": 1.0})
            rows.append(row)
            continue
        surfaced = {str(f.get("id")) for f in packet.get("facts") or []}
        row["hit"] = all(fact_id in surfaced for fact_id in task["relevant"])
        offset = raw.find('"facts"')
        row["prefix_fraction"] = (offset / len(raw)) if (offset >= 0 and raw) else 1.0
        rows.append(row)
    hits = sum(1 for r in rows if r["hit"])
    return {
        "tasks": len(rows),
        "hit_rate": (hits / len(rows)) if rows else 0.0,
        "max_prefix_fraction": max((r["prefix_fraction"] for r in rows), default=1.0),
        "mean_bytes": (sum(r["bytes"] for r in rows) / len(rows)) if rows else 0.0,
        "rows": rows,
    }


def measure(binary: Path, label: str, workdir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Seed a fresh store with `binary` and measure it. Raises ProbeError on contract breaks."""
    facts = load_json(FACTS_PATH)
    tasks = load_json(TASKS_PATH)
    if not binary.is_file():
        raise ProbeError(f"{label}: binary not found at {binary}")
    store = FixtureStore(workdir / label, facts["origin"], facts["branch"])
    store.create()
    ids = seed(store, binary, facts)

    expected = {fact_id for task in tasks for fact_id in task["relevant"]}
    seeded = set(ids.values())
    missing = sorted(expected - seeded)
    if missing:
        raise ProbeError(
            f"{label}: frozen task labels reference {len(missing)} fact id(s) the seeded store does not contain "
            f"(first: {missing[0]}); fact id derivation or the fixture changed, re-run `run.py freeze` deliberately"
        )

    summary = eval_facts(store, binary, TASKS_PATH)
    results = summary.get("results") or []
    labeled = [r for r in results if r.get("labeled")]
    mean_recall = (sum(float(r.get("recall", 0.0)) for r in labeled) / len(labeled)) if labeled else 0.0
    brief = brief_probe(store, binary, tasks)
    return {
        "label": label,
        "binary": str(binary),
        "facts_seeded": len(ids),
        "tasks": summary.get("tasks", 0),
        "tasks_sha256": (summary.get("run_config") or {}).get("tasks_sha256"),
        "brain_manifest_sha256": (summary.get("run_config") or {}).get("brain_manifest_sha256"),
        "mean_recall": mean_recall,
        "mean_precision": float(summary.get("mean_precision", 0.0)),
        "mean_useful_per_1k": float(summary.get("mean_useful_per_1k", 0.0)),
        "mean_tokens": float(summary.get("mean_tokens", 0.0)),
        "brief_hit_rate": brief["hit_rate"],
        "brief_max_prefix_fraction": brief["max_prefix_fraction"],
        "brief_mean_bytes": brief["mean_bytes"],
        "per_task": [
            {
                "id": r.get("id"),
                "recall": r.get("recall"),
                "precision": r.get("precision"),
                "useful_per_1k": r.get("useful_per_1k"),
                "tokens": r.get("tokens"),
            }
            for r in results
        ],
        "brief_rows": brief["rows"],
    }


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# scoring


def score(branch: dict[str, Any] | None, base: dict[str, Any] | None, error: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Turn measurements into the trail monitor value and rationale.

    value = 100 * min(branch mean recall, branch brief hit rate), floored to 0
    when the brief packet puts its facts past BRIEF_PREFIX_LIMIT of the bytes
    or when the measurement could not be made. Base deltas go in the rationale.
    """
    if error or branch is None:
        return {"value": 0, "rationale": f"Retrieval probe could not run: {error or 'no branch measurement'}"}

    recall = branch["mean_recall"]
    hit = branch["brief_hit_rate"]
    prefix = branch["brief_max_prefix_fraction"]
    value = int(round(100 * min(recall, hit)))
    flags: list[str] = []
    if prefix > BRIEF_PREFIX_LIMIT:
        value = 0
        flags.append(f"brief packet puts facts after {prefix:.0%} of its bytes (limit {BRIEF_PREFIX_LIMIT:.0%})")

    parts = [
        f"facts recall {recall:.0%}, precision {branch['mean_precision']:.2f}, "
        f"useful/1k {branch['mean_useful_per_1k']:.1f}, brief hit rate {hit:.0%} on {branch['tasks']} frozen tasks"
    ]
    if base is not None:
        d_recall = recall - base["mean_recall"]
        d_useful = branch["mean_useful_per_1k"] - base["mean_useful_per_1k"]
        d_prec = branch["mean_precision"] - base["mean_precision"]
        d_hit = hit - base["brief_hit_rate"]
        parts.append(
            f"vs base: recall {d_recall:+.0%}, precision {d_prec:+.2f}, useful/1k {d_useful:+.1f}, brief hit {d_hit:+.0%}"
        )
        if d_recall < 0 or d_hit < 0:
            flags.append("branch recovers fewer labeled facts than base")
        elif d_useful < -0.05 * max(base["mean_useful_per_1k"], 1e-9):
            flags.append("useful-per-1k fell more than 5% against base")
    if flags:
        parts.append("REGRESSION: " + "; ".join(flags))
    return {"value": value, "rationale": ". ".join(parts) + ".", "regressed": bool(flags)}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# building


def build(source: Path, output: Path) -> None:
    proc = run(["go", "build", "-o", str(output), "./cmd/entire-brain"], cwd=source, env=os.environ.copy(), timeout=900)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        raise ProbeError(f"go build in {source} failed: {proc.stderr.strip()[-400:]}")


def build_base(root: Path, base_ref: str, workdir: Path) -> Path:
    worktree = workdir / "base-src"
    env = git_env(os.environ.copy())
    proc = run(["git", "worktree", "add", "-q", "--detach", str(worktree), base_ref], cwd=root, env=env)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        raise ProbeError(f"git worktree add {base_ref} failed: {proc.stderr.strip()[:300]}")
    try:
        binary = workdir / "entire-brain-base"
        build(worktree, binary)
        return binary
    finally:
        run(["git", "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(worktree)], cwd=root, env=env)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# commands


def cmd_freeze(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    facts = load_json(FACTS_PATH)
    questions = load_json(QUESTIONS_PATH)
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="brain-retrieval-freeze-") as tmp:
        store = FixtureStore(Path(tmp) / "freeze", facts["origin"], facts["branch"])
        store.create()
        ids = seed(store, Path(args.bin).resolve(), facts)
    tasks = []
    for q in questions:
        unknown = [k for k in q["relevant_keys"] if k not in ids]
        if unknown:
            raise ProbeError(f"question {q['id']} names unknown fact key(s): {unknown}")
        tasks.append(
            {
                "id": q["id"],
                "task": q["task"],
                "branch": facts["branch"],
                "k": int(q.get("k", 5)),
                "relevant": [ids[k] for k in q["relevant_keys"]],
                "label_source": "human",
            }
        )
    TASKS_PATH.write_text(json.dumps(tasks, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"wrote {TASKS_PATH} ({len(tasks)} tasks, {len(ids)} facts, {sha256_file(TASKS_PATH)})")
    return 0


def cmd_measure(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="brain-retrieval-measure-") as tmp:
        try:
            report = measure(Path(args.bin).resolve(), "branch", Path(tmp))
            monitor = score(report, None)
        except ProbeError as exc:
            report, monitor = {"error": str(exc)}, score(None, None, str(exc))
    emit(report, monitor, args.json)
    return 0


def cmd_compare(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    root = repo_root()
    base_ref = args.base_ref or f"origin/{args.base_branch}"
    report: dict[str, Any] = {"fixture": {"facts": sha256_file(FACTS_PATH), "tasks": sha256_file(TASKS_PATH)}, "base_ref": base_ref}
    branch_m = base_m = None
    error = None
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="brain-retrieval-compare-") as tmp:
        work = Path(tmp)
        try:
            if args.branch_bin:
                branch_bin = Path(args.branch_bin).resolve()
            else:
                branch_bin = work / "entire-brain-branch"
                build(root, branch_bin)
            branch_m = measure(branch_bin, "branch", work)
            report["branch"] = branch_m
        except ProbeError as exc:
            error = str(exc)
            report["branch"] = {"error": error}
        if error is None:
            try:
                base_bin = Path(args.base_bin).resolve() if args.base_bin else build_base(root, base_ref, work)
                base_m = measure(base_bin, "base", work)
                report["base"] = base_m
            except ProbeError as exc:
                # A missing base is a weaker measurement, not a failed one.
                report["base"] = {"error": str(exc)}
    monitor = score(branch_m, base_m, error)
    if base_m is None and error is None:
        monitor["rationale"] += f" Base comparison unavailable: {report['base']['error'][:160]}."
    emit(report, monitor, args.json)
    return 0


def emit(report: dict[str, Any], monitor: dict[str, Any], compact: bool) -> None:
    """Report first, monitor object as the very last stdout line."""
    if not compact:
        print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
    print(json.dumps({"value": monitor["value"], "rationale": monitor["rationale"]}))


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    p = sub.add_parser("freeze", help="seed the fixture and write fixture/tasks.json with resolved fact ids")
    p.add_argument("--bin", required=True, help="entire-brain binary used to resolve fact ids")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_freeze)

    p = sub.add_parser("measure", help="measure one binary against the frozen fixture")
    p.add_argument("--bin", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="print only the monitor line")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_measure)

    p = sub.add_parser("compare", help="build HEAD and a base ref, measure both, print the monitor line last")
    p.add_argument("--base-branch", default="main", help="base branch name; the ref becomes origin/<name>")
    p.add_argument("--base-ref", help="explicit base ref (overrides --base-branch)")
    p.add_argument("--branch-bin", help="use this binary for HEAD instead of building")
    p.add_argument("--base-bin", help="use this binary for base instead of building")
    p.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="print only the monitor line")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_compare)

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        return int(args.func(args))
    except ProbeError as exc:
        print(json.dumps({"value": 0, "rationale": f"Retrieval probe could not run: {exc}"}))
        return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if shutil.which("git") is None:
        print(json.dumps({"value": 0, "rationale": "Retrieval probe could not run: git is not on PATH"}))
        sys.exit(2)
    sys.exit(main())
